body:
Part of #665 (Mark II split, plan stage S7). Depends on S6 (merged, dev-soft-core `1d6bf555`).

**Scope.** In the split build, MSRP (EtherType 0x22EA) and MVRP (0x88F5) leave through lwSRP's SRP channel TX ring, then `KL_mbx_tx`, then `ctl_tx_mux`, then the MAC. The split's licence register (`pub LICENCE`) drives the fabric policer. An lwSRP fix goes upstream to kebag-logic/lwSRP as a PR, never as a private copy.

**Acceptance.**
1. MRPDUs on the wire are well formed (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.8.1, 10.8.2): at most 1,500 octets, one Message per AttributeType (lwSRP PR #18), correct EndMarks.
2. Every MRPDU source address is the port's MAC from the first frame after reset (the #839 class, at the split).
3. At egress, JoinTime and LeaveAll spacing are within IEEE 802.1Q-2018 10.7.4 and Table 10-7 plus the approved service allowance (T_svc 20 ms).
4. With the TX ring full, no MRPDU is lost and order is kept. Backpressure reaches the firmware.
5. The #608 case: a withdrawal after a LeaveAll stops the talker.
6. The licence register reaches the policer in the split build exactly as in the all-fabric build.
7. Each check has a planted mutant that it kills: a malformed EndMark, a doubled declaration, LeaveAll on the wrong type, a frame dropped under backpressure, a zero source address.

**Measurements.** Egress interval error per MRP timer in simulation (µs, min/mean/max over N draws). Frames per transmit opportunity.

**Out of scope.** Ring geometry at 32x32 (#859, #865), the firmware loop structure (S2b), and bench confirmation (S12).
title: Mark II split S7: lwSRP's transmit path to the wire
